7.3.3.a
Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.

interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI Prostate (3T) showed a focal hypo-intense lesion in the left peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 x 10 mm, consistent with PI-RADS v2.1 category 4. The clinical T stage is cT1c.
**pathology_report**: Biopsy 1 from September 2024 revealed a focus of acinar adenocarcinoma in the peripheral zone, left side, with a Gleason score of 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). Perineural invasion was not present.
**previous_notes**: Notes confirm a prior diagnosis of ISUP grade group 2 prostate cancer, a PSA of 4.3 ng/mL in September 2024, and a prior biopsy performed on September 5, 2024.
**family_history**: Not recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trajectory shows an increase from 1.4 ng/mL in December 2023 to 6.2 ng/mL in January 2025.
**laboratory_results**: The most recent PSA is 6.2 ng/mL (as of December 16, 2024). Free PSA is 1.11 ng/mL (18%). Other labs (Hb, WBC, Creatinine, etc.) are within normal limits or not recorded.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The family history, and specific details regarding the trajectory of the PSA trend beyond the discrete points provided, are not fully recorded.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
The retrieved documents confirm a clinically significant finding: a PI-RADS 4 lesion on MRI and a confirmed ISUP grade group 2 adenocarcinoma on biopsy. The PSA has shown a clear upward trajectory. This evidence strongly supports the need for further discussion regarding the management pathway, as the findings are highly concerning for clinically significant prostate cancer.
